# Response Middleware

**Response Middleware** operates during the **outbound phase** of an HTTP request. Execution happens **after** `next()` returns, allowing the middleware to inspect or modify the `alfi::Response&` generated by downstream middleware or the target route handler.

---

## Response Processing Flow

Response middleware is ideal for post-processing operations, such as adding security headers, calculating response latency, compressing response data, or logging final status codes.

<!-- PLACEHOLDER: Image showing Response Middleware Execution Flow -->
![Response Middleware Execution Flow Placeholder](docs/images/response_middleware_flow.png)

```cpp
app.use([](const alfi::Request& req, alfi::Response& res, alfi::Next next) {
    // Phase 1: Inbound (Before next())
    // -------------------------------------------------------------
    
    next(); // Pass control to inner handlers/middleware
    
    // -------------------------------------------------------------
    // Phase 2: Outbound (After next())
    // Modifying res after handler execution
    res.header("X-Processed-By", "Alfi-Worker");
});
```

---

## Modifying Response Headers & Status

Response middleware can add, modify, or remove headers from the outgoing `alfi::Response&`:

### Example: Security Headers Middleware

```cpp
#include <alfi/app.hpp>

void security_headers_middleware(const alfi::Request& req, alfi::Response& res, alfi::Next next) {
    // Let handler process request
    next();

    // Attach security headers on outbound path
    res.header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff");
    res.header("X-Frame-Options", "DENY");
    res.header("X-XSS-Protection", "1; mode=block");
    res.header("Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains");
}

// Register globally
app.use(security_headers_middleware);
```

---

## Use Case: Execution Timing Middleware

Response middleware can measure total request execution duration by capturing a timestamp before calling `next()` and calculating elapsed time after `next()` completes:

```cpp
#include <alfi/app.hpp>
#include <chrono>
#include <iostream>

app.use([](const alfi::Request& req, alfi::Response& res, alfi::Next next) {
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

    // Execute downstream handlers
    next();

    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto durationMs = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(end - start).count() / 1000.0;

    // Attach timing header to response
    res.header("X-Response-Time", std::to_string(durationMs) + "ms");

    std::cout << "[Latency] " << req.method << " " << req.path 
              << " - " << res.statusCode << " (" << durationMs << " ms)" << std::endl;
});
```

---

## Important Considerations for Response Middleware

1. **Modify Response Object Directly**: Always mutate `res` in place (e.g., `res.header()`, `res.status()`).
2. **Order Matters**: Because response middleware logic runs after `next()`, response middleware registered **first** in `app.use()` will execute its post-`next()` block **last** (onion model).
3. **Handling Short-Circuits**: If an inner middleware short-circuits and does not call `next()`, outer response middleware post-`next()` code will still run for any outer layers whose `next()` was invoked.
